- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for 2–4 days.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.10) over 5+ days, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast for next 3–7 days.  
- Model frequently underestimates in early part of 30-day horizon (days 1–7); apply +0.5–1.5% bias to first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.  
- If sentiment turns sharply positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; increase forecast by 0.5–2% for next 3–5 days if sentiment > 0.15.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 20% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days unless sentiment supports continuation.  
- Lagged sentiment: if sentiment was positive 3–5 days ago, model often misses upward momentum; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–7 days.
